entities.summary: Caterina Assandra was an Italian composer and Benedictine nun. In her surviving motet book, Motetti a due a tre voci op.2, Assandra alludes to her birthplace being in the Province of Pavia. She became famous as an organist and published various works during her lifetime. Her work Motetti a due was dedicated to G.B. Biglia, the Bishop of Pavia, and was first recognized by publisher Lomazzo. Although Assandra had accumulated a substantial reputation for her works as a composer, even reaching outside the borders of Italy, she was at times confused with an 18th-century composer with the same name.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Caterina Assandra's compositions had a notable impact on Italian music during the Early Modern era, with her works being recognized by prominent figures of the time. Her publication in Lomazzo's catalog helped establish her reputation as an organist and composer.
